identificationModule.briefTitle: Standard Versus Intensity-Modulated Pelvic Radiation Therapy in Treating Patients With Endometrial or Cervical Cancer
identificationModule.officialTitle: A Randomized Phase III Study of Standard vs. IMRT Pelvic Radiation for Post-Operative Treatment of Endometrial and Cervical Cancer (TIME-C)

armGroups.label: Intensity-Modulated Radiation Therapy
armGroups.description: intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) to the pelvis of either 45 Gy or 50.4 Gy

armGroups.label: Standard Radiation Therapy
armGroups.description: Standard radiation therapy (4-field) to the pelvis of either 45 Gy or 50.4 Gy

interventions.name: Standard radiation therapy
interventions.description: Patients treated once a day, 5 days a week with a daily fraction size of 1.8 Gy. Whole pelvis treated with a four-field technique (AP/PA/R lateral/L lateral) to 45 or 50.4 Gy at 1.8 Gy/fraction. The dose is prescribed to the isocenter which is defined as the intersection of the four beams and can be normalized to an isodose line between 97-100%. The decision to deliver 45 or 50.4 Gy is at the physician's discretion and must be reported at the time of enrollment.

interventions.name: intensity-modulated radiation therapy
interventions.description: Patients treated once a day, 5 days a week with a daily fraction size of 1.8 Gy. All targets treated simultaneously. The vaginal planning target volume (PTV) (ITV with 7.0 mm margin) and nodal PTV receives 45 Gy in 25 fractions or 50.4 Gy in 28 fractions. The decision to deliver 45 or 50.4 Gy is at the physician's discretion and must be reported at the time of enrollment.
